sourceOfTruth: packages/vue-vscode/package.json and packages/vue-vscode/esbuild.config.mjs re-read live by tests/vscode-web/VSW0/vsw0.test.mjs
law: A build with only a Node main entry cannot pass as a web extension (VSW0-AC1). Web admission requires a real browser entrypoint and a browser-targeted build; contribution compatibility is declared per category, never assumed.

webAdmissionRules: the extension manifest must declare both main (Node extension host: desktop and remote) and browser (web extension host) entries; main-only is not a web extension and browser-only is not the desktop product
the browser entry bundle must target the browser platform and import no Node builtins and no vscode-languageclient/node (the Node transport stays desktop-owned per VSC0 transport-desktop-owned)
the web entry never spawns a child process, never reads fs/os/process, and reaches native capability only through the explicitly selected companion route

the browser entry lives at packages/vue-vscode/src/browser and host-neutral modules at packages/vue-vscode/src/shared: a sibling consumer of the same producers, never a fork of the desktop extension (VSC0 browser-is-distinct-product)
admission is a build predicate re-derived from the live manifest and build config, not a claim stamped at packaging time

contributions.rule: declarative language contributions ship unchanged from either entry (vue, svelte, vue-html, vue-postcss, vue-sugarss with their configuration files)
TextMate grammars and injectTo rules are static assets; identical in web mode

command declarations are shared, but each command's implementation binds its WebExtensionFeatureContract row: a command whose producer is remote-native-only or companion-route surfaces the HostStatusVocabulary status for its surface, never a silent no-op or a dropped registration
declarative when-clauses; the context keys they reference (view == verterVirtualFiles, viewItem == virtual-file) are set by whichever entry is active
the verter-analysis activity-bar container is declarative

view declarations are shared, but their when-clauses (verter.analysisEnabled, verter.hasActiveCarrierFile) must be set by the web entry too; a view that cannot be populated in a mode is not registered in that mode (no permanently empty views)
theme color contributions are declarative and identical in web mode

settings are shared, but node-bound settings (verter.lspBinaryPath, verter.typescript.tsdk, verter.statistics.persistToFile, verter.statistics.filePath, verter.viteConfig.trustedFiles, verter.mcp.*) declare their web behavior: unsupported or companion-scoped per the HostStatusVocabulary, never silently ignored
editor defaults for vue/svelte are declarative

the plugin runs inside the editor-owned TypeScript engine wherever that engine runs (ExternalOwner); on the web the built-in TypeScript service uses its own web worker — no Node enters Verter's closure through this contribution; compatibility is owned by VSW3

the definition registers a spawned verter-mcp child; browser-local mode has no process capability, so the definition is registered only when the companion (VSW4N) or a remote-native host is actually serving — never a dead definition
onLanguage (6), onView (2) and onCommand (3) activations are host-neutral and drive the same activation gate from either entry

rules: contribution categories cover exactly the live package.json contributes keys plus activationEvents; a new contribution category without a compatibility row is drift
liveCount values are re-derived from the live manifest by the harness; count drift is a failing case, not a stale pass
host-neutral and entry-bound contributions ship in both entries; engine-following contributions follow the editor-owned engine; web-incompatible contributions are conditional on a live serving host
packaging a web build while this policy's liveState verdict is not-admitted: node-main-only is forbidden; VSW5 owns the packaging gate that enforces it
